nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How can presenting cell-based meat and seafood as unprocessed and whole help change consumer perceptions?
nodes.answer: By presenting CBM/S as steaks or fish fillets, negative perceptions around over-processing can be reduced, potentially improving acceptance.

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Which stages are analyzed in the value chain of seafood?
nodes.answer: The stages analyzed include catching, distribution, processing, and commercialization of seafood.

On the other hand, the enlargement of harbour-based fisheries economic analysis to a broader economic impact analysis has been done mainly through regional input out- put models (Garza-Gil et al. 2017; Garc a-de-la-Fuente et al. 2020; Raffray et al. 2022), computable general equilibrium models (Akbari et al. 2023), and value chain analyses (de la Puente and Christensen 2024). This latter type of analy - sis is used to understand how the wealth (and sometimes employment) generated by an economic activity is distrib- uted among the different stakeholders involved, from the beginning of the activity to its completion. In the case of fisheries, the aim is to better understand the impact, in mon- etary and employment terms, at each stage through which seafood moves from the boat to the plate, including catching, distribution, processing, and commercialization. Value chain has been widely used all over the world in very different contexts (Gudmundsson et al. 2006; Failler et al. 2014; FAO and Neven 2014; Khan and Chuenpagdee 2014; Pascual- Fernandez et al.

nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What does the value chain module describe in relation to seafood products?
nodes.answer: The value chain module describes the flow of seafood products from fishers to consumers, including the associated revenues, costs, salaries, and employment for all stakeholders in the value chain.
nodes.paragraph: These parameters were used as inputs in the value chain module that describe the flow of seafood products from fishers to consumers and the associated rev - enues, costs, salaries, and employment for all stakeholders in the value chain (Christensen et al. 2011). The value chain model consisted of 16 different main enterprise types, whose main linkages are depicted in Fig. 2 (see Supplementary material 2.1 for more information on the data for the value chain). The value chain structure was defined using previous fish value chain reports developed in Spain (Tragsatec 2011, 2012a, b, C; Garc a Antoni 2012; EUMOFA 2015; Cam 2020 ; Ortega Cerd and Coll 2022a ; Ortega Cerd et al. 2023; Ram rez and Sarroca 2023; Moranta et al. 2023) and was checked to ensure fulfilness and adequacy in fora with the participation of the main stakeholders of the area (Mas- carell-Rocher 2021; Ortega Cerd and Coll 2022b; Ortega Cerd et al. 2023). Most of the value chain operates as a fresh supply chain within the national market, with very low processing levels.
